title: Request provenance signer: deterministic provenance header + compat middleware for SDKs
creator: Ava Moreno
description: Introduce a lightweight, deterministic `X-RW-Provenance` header produced by Redwood SDKs and middleware to validate end-to-end request provenance and reduce lost/duplicated traces across proxies and retries. This ticket covers design and delivery of: 1) a signer algorithm compatible with existing propagation headers (traceparent/baggage/otlp), 2) SDK integrations (Node/Python/Go) that emit the header without adding blocking crypto latencies, 3) middleware for edge proxies and the runtime to validate and attach provenance metadata to spans, and 4) a fallback reconciliation path for older clients that don't emit the header.
tasks: Design deterministic provenance header format and signing primitives (HMAC-SHA256 truncated) - RFC draft
Prototype verifier middleware for edge-proxy (fast path in Rust) and runtime ingress
Implement Node SDK: non-blocking signer with optional in-memory key cache
Implement Python SDK: async-compatible signer using threaded pool for HMAC
Implement Go SDK: signer that uses crypto/hmac and reuses buffers
Add runtime span enrichment to attach provenance validation result and origin hint
Integration tests: cross-language request roundtrip with retries and sampling changes
Backward-compat reconciliation: heuristics to stitch traces when header missing
Add console dashboard panel for provenance-valid vs unknown vs invalid traces
Security review and KMS key rotation plan
acceptance_criteria: SDKs emit X-RW-Provenance header for instrumented requests by default
Edge-proxy middleware validates header and attaches provenance.ok=true to span attributes for valid tokens
End-to-end integration tests pass with simulated retries and proxy hops
No request-path p95 latency regression > 2ms for common fast-path (Node SDK + Rust proxy) under load
Console dashboard shows provenance state breakdown and alerts for sudden drops in valid provenance rate
updates: 2026-02-20: Kickoff meeting — agreed on HMAC-SHA256 truncate(12) as signer primitive to keep header small and verification cheap.
2026-02-24: Prototype Rust middleware built; single-CPU verification cost ~0.8us for HMAC check; good perf headroom.
2026-03-01: Node SDK approach chosen: use WebCrypto/HMAC when available, fallback to native accelerated binding. Avoid synchronous filesystem KMS calls.
2026-03-04: Decided to include a 4-bit origin hint in header (sdk-lang:node/python/go + version) to help analytics; will be truncated in privacy mode.
2026-03-08: Validation logic updated to accept 'rotated' keys for a 24-hour grace window; added to design doc.
2026-03-10: PRs open: rust-proxy#412, sdk-node#227, sdk-go#166. Integration test harness running in CI; intermittent flakes when sampling boundary crosses retry — investigating.
risks: Risk: naive signing could add CPU cost at high QPS; Mitigation: use truncated HMAC and vectorized implementations in Rust/Go, batch verification in ingress worker
Risk: header leaks PII or identifiable payload; Mitigation: provenance signer covers request metadata only (trace ids + non-sensitive method/route hash), design excludes payload or user identifiers
Risk: interoperability with legacy clients; Mitigation: reconciliation heuristics and gradual rollout with opt-in flag followed by default-on after 6 weeks
Risk: key management complexity; Mitigation: use KMS with short-lived keys, server-side rotation with grace window, and async fetch in SDKs
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable middleware and runtime validation for 5% of hosted API traffic; SDKs opt-in via env var
Phase 2 (gradual): SDK default-on in minor releases; increase runtime validation to 50% with fallback stitching enabled
Phase 3 (enforce): runtime rejects prov-invalid requests for internal-only routes and surfaces metric/alert; full enforcement after 8 weeks
Post-rollout: monitor provenance.valid_rate, trace connect rate, and p95 ingress latencies; rollback knob prepared
